entry.summary: Measurement-induced entanglement phases in hyperbolic gauge-Higgs models arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies entanglement phases of gauge-Higgs models on hyperbolic lattices, described by measurement-only dynamics. The authors map two-dimensional phase diagrams using topological entanglement entropy and a generalized measurement-induced entanglement suited to hyperbolic Higgs phases. They identify an "archipelago" phase absent in Euclidean space, where separated clusters of symmetry-protected topological order exist, and its transitions have mean-field critical exponents.

entry.title: Fewest Measurement Settings for Estimating Several Quantum Observables
entry.summary: Minimal Projective Measurement Settings for Estimating Multiple Observables arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies the minimum number of orthogonal projective measurement settings needed to estimate several observables without bias for any input state. The authors derive structural lower bounds beyond dimension counting and give explicit constructions that certify minimum setting counts for chosen target spaces. A classical variational algorithm searches for shared measurement bases and optimizes readout coefficients and sample allocation. For the collective first and second moments of two qubits, four projective settings are shown to be both necessary and sufficient.

entry.title: Unusual shapes of Fisher zero lines in biorthogonal dynamical quantum phase transitions
entry.summary: Anomalous Structures of Fisher Zero Lines in Biorthogonal Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how Fisher zero lines of the Loschmidt amplitude in non-Hermitian quenches can form unusual patterns in the complex time plane, such as divergence, separation, or branches lying on the real or imaginary axis. It uses a biorthogonal framework to explain these patterns and sets critical momentum conditions based on the dot product of normalized prequench and postquench complex Bloch vectors. The results are verified in a generalized non-Hermitian SSH model, and Jordan form is used to analyze dynamics at postquench exceptional points.

entry.title: Dynamical behaviour of the mass tensor in the lattice
entry.summary: Dynamical behaviour of the mass tensor in the lattice arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies, with a semiclassical model, how a particle hopping through an orthorhombic lattice moves under a static Coulomb field and a rapidly oscillating homogeneous field. Applying the oscillating field reparameterizes the effective masses so they become equal in both directions, turning a chaotic trajectory into an elliptic one in the continuum limit, as confirmed by Lyapunov exponents. The authors also show that an external magnetic field along the Z direction can control chaos, and extend the scheme to three-dimensional trajectories.

entry.title: Coherent optical control of a single donor electron spin
entry.summary: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper demonstrates optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton transitions and off-resonant picosecond pulses, the authors observe spin Rabi oscillations, Ramsey interference, and high-contrast coherent population trapping. At higher driving strengths, multiple dark resonances reveal the hyperfine interaction with the I = 3/2 Cl nucleus, and the authors identify isolated optical donors as a promising platform for solid-state optically active qubits. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report optical initialization and coherent control of a single donor electron spin in ZnSe, with coherent population trapping and hyperfine interaction with the Cl nucleus revealed by mult

entry.title: Analytic energy formulas for radial power-like potentials via new Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions
entry.summary: Radial power-like potentials: from the Bohr-Sommerfeld ℓ ≠ 0 state energies to the exact ones arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper proposes two new Bohr-Sommerfeld type quantization conditions for d-dimensional radial singular and non-singular potentials. It studies power-like potentials and the logarithmic potential across many radial quantum numbers and angular momenta in dimensions two and three. For large radial quantum numbers the approximate energies approach the exact ones, and a dimensionless WKB correction reproduces exact energies within the cases examined.

entry.title: Sideways position shift of a spinning particle's wave packet under Lorentz boosts
entry.summary: Side jump and anomalous Lorentz transformation of a coherent Dirac wave packet arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how spin-orbit coupling makes the average position of a spinning particle shift unusually under a Lorentz boost, an effect called a side jump. The authors develop a trace method that yields an exact, compact transformation kernel for the probability center of a general three-dimensional Dirac wave packet under any finite boost, without a semiclassical expansion. They find that side jumps depend on the wave packet's internal structure and that, for Gaussian packets, they show a non-monotonic dependence on mass.

entry.title: Consensus and information spreading in quantum networks: how nodes learn global quantum information from local measurements
entry.summary: Consensus And Information Redistribution In Quantum Networks arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies decentralized quantum consensus in qudit networks evolving under discrete random unitary dynamics. The authors analyze asymptotic behavior, identify global information preserved by the evolution, and give conditions under which different forms of quantum consensus arise. They present a general theorem for extracting globally encoded information from local measurements, examine CNOT networks, and identify two-qubit interactions that asymptotically reach consensus on average excitation number.

entry.title: Finite-temperature quantum theory of lossy magnon-cavity resonators
entry.summary: Finite-temperature Quantum Quasinormal Mode Theory for Spatiotemporally-resolved Dissipative Cavity Quantum Magnonics arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper develops a finite-temperature quantum quasinormal mode (QNM) theory for cavity magnonic systems containing non-reciprocal magnetic media, material dissipation, open-cavity radiation losses and thermal fluctuations. It uses macroscopic quantum electrodynamics and complex coordinate transformations to quantize the QNMs. The authors apply the theory to hybrid dielectric-magnonic resonators coupled to spin and superconducting qubits, showing modal interference, a transition from coherent to dissipative coupling, and magnon-mediated qubit synchronization.

entry.title: Suppressing microwave crosstalk in superconducting quantum processors by designing parasitic capacitances
entry.summary: Suppressing microwave crosstalk in superconducting quantum processors by designing parasitic drive capacitances arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how unwanted microwave drive crosstalk between qubits in a superconducting quantum processor can be reduced. The authors build a detailed circuit model of a processor with two fixed-frequency transmon qubits and a tunable coupler, and experimentally show that crosstalk can be suppressed. They find the suppression comes not only from cancelling the effective qubit-qubit coupling but also from interference among other coupling paths. The authors conclude that choosing suitable parasitic capacitances can suppress crosstalk, suggesting that parasitic coupling paths should be engineered rather than simply minimized.

entry.title: Multi-day magnetic imaging of single living cancer cells using a quantum sensor
entry.summary: Multi-day single-cell magnetic imaging of living cancer cells using Quantum Cell Monitoring arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents Quantum Cell Monitoring (QCM), a widefield nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry platform that records single-cell information from stray magnetic fields instead of emitted photons, at subcellular resolution. Combined with a live-cell incubator, it tracks magnetically labeled living cancer cells for up to 72 hours. The authors report observing mitosis, morphological changes, and cluster formation, splitting, and migration.

entry.title: Upper bounds on how often feedback-controlled quantum trajectories exceed quantum speed limits
entry.summary: Probability bounds on trajectory-level exceedances of quantum speed limits under continuous-measurement feedback arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies the probability that a single conditioned quantum trajectory, under continuous measurement feedback, exceeds a quantum speed limit (QSL) velocity derived from an ensemble. Using the finite-time average fidelity velocity, the authors bound this exceedance probability in terms of its mean and variance, and obtain state-independent bounds, including an exponential concentration bound. For a feedback-controlled qubit they give explicit model-specific bounds that are nontrivial at short times. They also identify a finite-time regime where the exceedance probability is exactly zero because the conditioned dynamics have restricted support. Monte Carlo simulations confirm the analytical bounds and show their tightness.

entry.title: Preparing Geometric States on the Bloch Sphere with a Linear Mechanical Resonator
entry.summary: Experimental Geometric State Preparation on the Bloch Sphere Via Linear Mechanical Resonator arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper applies the Bloch sphere representation, familiar from quantum two-level systems, to a linear two-mass, three-spring mechanical system. The system is driven from both ends at a fixed frequency between its two resonances, producing tunable superpositions of its symmetric and antisymmetric modes. Laser vibrometer measurements and frequency-domain analysis are used to extract the modal coefficients and map them onto Bloch sphere coordinates. The results show planar rotations under phase sweeps and continuous steering between eigenstates under amplitude-ratio tuning.

entry.title: Quantum fluid dynamics built on Nambu's unpublished fluid notes
entry.summary: Quantum hydrodynamics from Nambu's unpublished fluid notes arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper develops a quantum hydrodynamic theory based on an unpublished note by Nambu on fluid dynamics. Tracing out unobserved fluid modes yields a quantum channel for an observed cyclic deformation, and a criterion is given for exact preservation of coherence between opposite momenta. Using two shear flows as an example, the authors identify an exact noiseless sign subsystem and show that a preparation with smaller initial decoherence can still suffer larger maximum loss over a finite readout interval.

entry.title: Quantum computing study of bulk FeO ground-state properties
entry.summary: Towards Quantum Computation of Bulk FeO arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies the ground-state properties of molecular FeO and Fe2O2 model Hamiltonians using classical exact diagonalization, the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD). The experimentally known quintet ground state of FeO is recovered both classically and with quantum algorithms, and a nonet ground state is found for Fe2O2. Raw VQE does not reach chemical accuracy, but SQD with two connectivity shells recovers the exact ground energy for both molecules using very few quantum resources.

entry.title: Semiconductor quantum dot produces quantum light with adjustable Wigner negativity
entry.summary: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This study uses a single semiconductor quantum dot inside a cavity to generate quantum light states with tunable Wigner negativity. Optical coherent control of the dot's transition creates a superposition of zero and one photon, which is characterized point by point in phase space via homodyne measurement. Wigner-function negativity appears as excitation power increases. After correcting for collection and propagation losses, fidelities to the ideal state and quantum purities exceed 95%.

entry.title: Ultrafast light-electron modulation for free-electron quantum optics
entry.summary: Ultrafast light-electron modulation for free-electron quantum optics: fundamentals and applications arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a unified Light-Electron Modulation (LEM) framework that treats optical near fields as programmable phase modulators for free-electron wavepackets. It identifies longitudinal energy and transverse momentum modulation channels and describes how their operation depends on wavepacket extent, recoil, phase matching, and field geometry. The authors show that PINEM, Raman-Nath and Bragg diffraction, DLA-like acceleration, and anomalous PINEM can be organized as limiting regimes of one modulation picture, and they derive design principles for free-electron modulators.

entry.title: Optical tensor processing for simulating quantum circuits
entry.summary: Quantum circuit simulation with high-order optical tensor processing arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents a classical optical architecture for quantum circuit simulation that treats gates and input-state batches as independent tensor dimensions and maps eligible tensor network contractions onto the same processor. Using multidimensional encoding and readout across spatial and wavelength degrees of freedom, the authors experimentally realize high-order tensor-matrix multiplication in a single propagation for all computational-basis inputs of a 4-qubit gate. A physics-based optical propagation model is used to numerically evaluate the approach for the Deutsch algorithm and a tensor network covering all 128 target instances of a 7-qubit Grover algorithm.

entry.title: Analog quantum experiments with automatic differentiation: from programs to atoms
entry.summary: Analog Quantum Experiments Meet Automatic Differentiation - from Programs to Atoms arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces DiffSimuQ, a method that applies automatic differentiation to a broad class of open-loop analog quantum experiments. It transforms an experiment program into a derivative program whose expected outcome equals the gradient. For continuous evolution it gives two realizations, the Nyquist shift rule for general time-dependent evolution and a parameter-shift realization for involutory generators. In noisy emulation, both avoid the finite-difference error floor and improve closed-loop optimization.

entry.title: Estimating entanglement in many-body states from partial-transpose moments
entry.summary: Many-body entanglement quantification in arbitrary states through a few partial-transpose moments arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper shows how the logarithmic negativity, a measure of entanglement, can be estimated for an arbitrary many-body state without reconstructing the state. It uses a finite number of even partial transpose moments and solves a truncated Hausdorff moment problem with Gauss and Gauss-Radau quadrature. The resulting lower bounds improve as the moment order increases and are illustrated on ground states of three interacting spin models and a thermal state, with an error analysis for finite statistics. ★★★★ Notable: Using finitely many even partial-transpose moments and a truncated Hausdorff moment problem, the authors derive progressively tightening lower bounds on logarithmic negativity, illustrated on spin-mod

entry.title: Non-Hermitian Schwinger effect in imaginary magnetic fields
entry.summary: Non-Hermitian Schwinger effect in an imaginary magnetic field arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The authors analyze the one-loop effective Lagrangian of scalar and Dirac QED in a real electric field combined with a parallel imaginary magnetic field. They show that the imaginary magnetic field adds an extra pole family to the proper-time integrand and can produce a nonzero imaginary part even without an electric field. When the field-strength ratio is rational, some poles coincide and require careful treatment.

entry.title: Algebraic characterisation of invariants for n-qubit pure states
entry.summary: An algebraic characterisation of n-qubit pure-state invariants arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies n-qubit pure quantum states written as density matrices in Bloch representation. The authors define a family of quadratic functions of Pauli expectation values and fully determine which choices yield state-independent purity constraints. The resulting invariants are closely tied to the geometry of symplectic polar spaces. A subfamily stable under state updates is shown to correspond to symplectic Lie algebras generated by Pauli operators.

entry.title: Training quantum circuits by learning from equilibrium states of a physical model
entry.summary: Equilibrium Learning of Quantum Circuits arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper extends equilibrium learning, which trains physical systems using observables of their relaxed states, to gate-based quantum circuits. A parametrized circuit is embedded in a Feynman-Kitaev Hamiltonian, and the compilation target is imposed via an output clamping term or a target-dependent cyclic condition on the clock register. Cost functions for unitary and state compilation are defined using ground state energies and overlaps with the free history state. In two-qubit benchmarks, optimization with these equilibrium costs reaches a fixed fidelity threshold in fewer sweeps than the standard compilation infidelity cost for many instances.

entry.title: Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling: an efficient method for quantum trajectories in metastable open systems
entry.summary: Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling for efficient quantum trajectories in metastable open quantum systems arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper introduces DiSLOU, a method for efficiently simulating quantum trajectories in open quantum systems that exhibit metastability. It combines three optimization layers: switching among locally optimal unravelings that minimize quantum jumps, diagonalizing the non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian once per attractor to speed up no-jump evolution, and propagating states in a truncated subspace of slowly decaying eigenmodes. The method is tested on a driven-dissipative Kerr resonator, with the largest speedup in the bistable regime, and applied to rare bit-flip events in the cat manifold of a dissipatively stabilized parametric oscillator, where it gives over an order of magnitude improvement.

entry.title: Interactions between spin-like states in ultracold molecules, a step toward precision tests of physics
entry.summary: Parity-doublet spin interactions in ultracold polyatomic molecules arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper reports observing and controlling resonant dipolar exchange interactions between parity-doublet states in ultracold polyatomic CaOH molecules held in an optical trap. The researchers encode a pseudospin in these states and detect density-dependent loss of Ramsey contrast and a mean-field precession whose sign reverses with the initial population imbalance. Floquet engineering of the interaction anisotropy suppresses many-body dephasing near the SU(2)-symmetric Heisenberg point. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first observation and control of resonant dipolar exchange in parity doublets of ultracold CaOH molecules, state that one discrete truncated Wigner model describes both the Rams

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Conditional Mutual Information in Random Classical Systems
entry.summary: Universal Scaling of Conditional Mutual Information in Classical Stochastic Dynamics arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how conditional mutual information (CMI), which measures dependence between two regions given an intervening buffer, evolves in one-dimensional classical stochastic models. The authors propose a universal scaling form for systems whose Markov length grows with time and derive it in the inactive phase of parity-conserving directed percolation. A Hankel-based truncation scheme enables matrix-product-state simulations that verify the scaling. The CMI between fixed microscopic regions is found to share a common scaling dimension of two.

entry.title: Mesons, Confinement, and Krylov Complexity in a Long-Range Ising Chain
entry.summary: Mesons, Confinement, and Complexity: A Krylov Space Perspective on the Long-Range Ising Chain arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how confinement and Krylov complexity are linked in a long-range transverse-field Ising chain, where power-law interactions create an effective confining potential between domain walls. Using the time-averaged Krylov state complexity after a quench as a diagnostic, the complexity is strongly suppressed at small α and small transverse field, and grows rapidly at larger α. In the confined regime, the oscillation frequencies match the meson masses of an effective two-kink model.

entry.title: Typical entanglement growth and transport fluctuations in a quantum exclusion model
entry.summary: Typicality of entanglement growth and transport fluctuations in quantum symmetric exclusion processes arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies the quantum symmetric exclusion process, a model of randomly hopping free fermions with diffusive transport and long-range quantum coherence, using macroscopic fluctuation theory. The authors show that charge-transfer statistics for individual noise realizations almost surely match those of the classical symmetric exclusion process at long times, both in equilibrium and after quenches from diagonal product states. They also derive asymptotically exact predictions for entanglement growth from domain-wall and Néel initial states, which agree well with numerical simulations.

entry.title: Symmetry-resolved fermionic correlations in iron-oxide ground spaces
entry.summary: Symmetry-resolved fermionic correlations in iron-oxide ground spaces arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies how symmetries organize degenerate ground states in many-body electronic models of FeO and Fe2O2. Resolving the same degenerate ground space with different symmetry operators yields states with very different correlation properties. With density-density Hund interactions added, the FeO ground space reduces to a spin-reversal pair with maximal magnetization.

entry.title: An open effective field theory for dark matter searches with matter-wave interferometers
entry.summary: An open EFT for dark matter searches with matter-wave interferometers arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper treats matter-wave interferometers as open quantum systems coupled to a dark matter environment and derives an open effective field theory using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. The framework describes two signatures, dark matter-induced phase shifts and loss of contrast. The authors analyze elastic spin-independent sub-GeV dark matter scattering off nucleons and discuss the regions of parameter space that composite-particle interferometers could probe for Higgs-portal and light hadrophilic scalar mediated dark matter.

entry.title: An analytic bootstrap method for solving quantum mechanics of a particle on a circle
entry.summary: Analytic Bootstrap Solution for Quantum Mechanics on a Circle arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper solves the Schrödinger equation for a particle on a circle using a quantum mechanical bootstrap approach. It requires the solutions of recursion relations for Fourier coefficients to vanish exponentially fast, yielding a generalized continued fraction representation that is analytic in the couplings and energy. The authors show how to compute the density of states, reconstruct the wave function, and extract quasimomentum versus energy. Applied to the Mathieu equation, the method resolves exponentially small bands in the spectrum.

entry.title: AlgebrasTQD: A Tool for Computing Algebras and Interfaces in Twisted Quantum Doubles
entry.summary: AlgebrasTQD: Computing Algebras and Interfaces in Twisted Quantum Doubles arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents AlgebrasTQD, an open-source GAP program for computing condensable algebras and their topological boundaries and interfaces in twisted quantum doubles. It can classify 1+1d gapped and gapless phases related to a finite group by gauging, study 2+1d anyon proliferation, and construct logical gates in non-Abelian topological codes. The paper illustrates its use with several Abelian and non-Abelian groups and states that all arithmetic is exact.

entry.title: A paper linking qubit- and boson-based quantum sensing methods for detecting new physics
entry.summary: A Correspondence Between Qubit- and Boson-Based Sensing Protocols arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper uses the Holstein–Primakoff transformation to unify qubit-based and boson-based sensing proposals within one framework. It introduces a novel generalization of GHZ states that performs better at detecting rare interactions, and states these states can be readily prepared while combining GHZ coherence with improved error rejection. It also extends the Hamiltonian-Not-in-Lindblad-Span theorem to collections of bosonic modes.

entry.title: How amorphization depth affects bismuth redistribution and activation in silicon for quantum devices
entry.summary: Amorphization-Depth-Dependent Bismuth Redistribution and Activation in Silicon for Quantum Devices arXiv · Oct 26, 2026The study compares 20 keV bismuth implantation directly into silicon with implantation after silicon preamorphization. The two routes produce amorphous layers of about 47 nm and 177 ± 15 nm deep. After annealing at 650 °C for 300 s, substitutional Bi fractions are similar (91 ± 2% and 89 ± 4%), but Hall-derived electrical activation is about 60% and 90%. The results show that amorphization depth and regrowth geometry govern Bi redistribution and affect electrical activation beyond substitutional incorporation alone.

entry.title: A solvable obstructed seam on a lattice Klein bottle, and how register choice affects toric codes
entry.summary: An exactly solvable obstructed seam on a lattice Klein bottle: bulk-locked Majorana rings and register-dependent toric codes arXiv · Oct 20, 2026The paper studies a frustrated seam formed by reflection-gluing Wen's plaquette model on a closed lattice Klein bottle. Its seam operators reduce to free Majorana rings, and bulk stabilizers restrict the allowed sectors, yielding exact ground energies, gaps and degeneracies. It contrasts this with consistent toric-code realizations using an edge register, which preserves anyon labels, and a Hadamard-dressed site register, which has colour-dependent seam transport.

entry.title: Quantum circuits for elastic wave equations using Schrödingerisation
entry.summary: Quantum circuits of elastic wave equations via Schrödingerisation arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper builds explicit quantum circuits for the velocity-stress form of elastic wave equations in homogeneous media, using Schrödingerisation. The equations are rewritten in symmetric matrix form, with Fourier spectral discretization for periodic problems and staggered-grid finite differences for physical boundaries. The authors analyze splitting errors and CNOT-gate counts for higher-order Trotter-Suzuki formulas and compare with classical partitioned splitting, finding a polynomial improvement in spatial-resolution dependence. Noiseless circuit simulations illustrate the constructions and quantify errors against exact and classical reference solutions.

entry.title: Matrix samplers and quantum-proof extractors: equivalence and near-optimal constructions
entry.summary: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions arXiv · Oct 27, 2026The paper establishes an equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors, extending Zuckerman's classical sampler-extractor correspondence. Using this equivalence, the authors construct explicit strong matrix samplers with optimal randomness overhead and near-optimal sample complexity. They also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors with improved seed and output lengths. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show matrix samplers and quantum-proof extractors are equivalent, and use this to build explicit strong matrix samplers with fewer samples and shorter seeds than prior work.

entry.title: Quantum evolution kernel for embedding attributed graphs on neutral-atom computers
entry.summary: Quantum Evolution Kernel for Node-Attributed Graphs arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a way to embed node-attributed graphs on neutral-atom quantum computers and applies it to digit recognition. It extends PASQAL's quantum evolution kernel with a node-level encoding based on three-level quantum states, and uses the resulting correlation-based information for classification. The quantum process is simulated with the Pulser library, which limits dataset size. On digit recognition, the method using the Wasserstein distance achieves higher mean accuracy than commonly used Jensen-Shannon distance-based methods.

entry.title: Circuit-aware mutation testing for quantum programs: exact visibility and execution planning
entry.summary: Toward Circuit-Aware Mutation Testing for Quantum Programs: Exact Visibility and Execution Planning arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper proposes a circuit-aware framework for mutation testing of quantum programs, distinguishing whether surviving mutants leave behavior unchanged, are hidden by input or measurement choices, or lack sufficient statistical evidence. It targets ideal, noiseless programs with mutations that replace one gate or subcircuit, combining mathematical checks with statistical estimates. For supported cases, it gives conditions under which a test cannot reveal a mutation and exact effect formulas, along with a decision procedure, guarantees, and a small-circuit reference implementation.

entry.title: Lifting Quasi-Cyclic Additive Codes to Certified Quantum Codes
entry.summary: Ancestor Lifting of Quasi-Cyclic Additive Codes and Certified Quantum Codes arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper studies additive codes over F4 that correspond to binary quantum stabilizer codes, focusing on 1-generator (1,2)-quasi-cyclic additive codes. It gives an ancestor-lifting theorem for composite lengths, dimension laws, and a palindromic criterion for symplectic self-orthogonality. Exact quantum distances are determined through information-set decoding screening, Brouwer–Zimmermann computation, and independent witness verification. The authors certify a set of record-breaking binary quantum codes and report further propagated entries and upper bounds.

entry.title: Tensor-train method for simulating quantum system dynamics in phase space
entry.summary: Dynamical Tensor Train Approximation for Wigner--Fokker--Planck Equation with Applications to Open Quantum Systems arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper presents a dynamical tensor-train method for solving the Wigner–Fokker–Planck equation, which describes continuous-variable open quantum systems. The Wigner function is evolved directly in tensor-train form using a projector-splitting integrator, and the nonlocal Wigner pseudo-differential operator is handled with low-rank representations and matrix-free exponential actions. Numerical experiments in one, two, and three spatial dimensions show the method's accuracy and scalability, including simulations in a six-dimensional phase space.

entry.title: Scaling and renormalization theory applied to grokking in neural networks
entry.summary: Scaling and Renormalization in Neural Networks: An Effective Renormalization-Group Description of Grokking arXiv · Oct 27, 2026This paper examines whether scaling and renormalization group theories can describe grokking, the delayed shift from memorization to generalization in deep neural networks. Using a two-layer network trained on modular addition, the authors define an order parameter and fluctuation measures, then apply real-space renormalization with a coupling matrix to derive five critical exponents. The reported direct empirical estimates match the theoretical predictions within 1 to 10 percent, and the authors propose this formalism as a tool for studying neural network dynamics.

entry.title: Preparing large cat states efficiently with optical operations
entry.summary: Generation of large-amplitude squeezed cat states with near-unity efficiency arXiv · Sep 30, 2026The paper proposes an all-optical scheme that uses quantum non-demolition interactions and photon-number measurements to prepare large-amplitude cat states with near-unity probability. No particular photon-number outcome is postselected; every outcome adds to the accumulated photon number, and the protocol repeats until a required threshold is reached. The authors show the scheme is robust to realistic photon loss, the dominant error source in optical systems.

entry.title: Optical realization of a cavity field with uniformly moving mirrors
entry.summary: Photonic realization of an electromagnetic cavity field with uniform mirror motion arXiv · Oct 11, 2026This paper mathematically studies the effective Hamiltonian of a non-stationary electromagnetic cavity field with uniform linear mirror motion, introduced by C. K. Law. The authors reinterpret bosonic coupling terms as generators of the symplectic algebra Sp(4,R), which can be implemented with linear optical elements, allowing strong effective interactions. They derive analytical expressions for the average photon number in each mode and show generation of two-mode squeezed states. Statistical properties such as intermode correlations, the Mandel parameter, and linear entropy are analyzed, and the Wigner function visualizes the system's behavior in phase space.

entry.title: Comparing zero- and infinite-temperature damping in variational quantum circuits, covering feature scale, sampling cost, and frame gauge
entry.summary: Zero- Versus Infinite-Temperature Damping in Variational Quantum Circuits: Feature Scale, Sampling Cost, and Frame Gauge arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper compares amplitude damping with its Pauli-twirled version, which is generalized amplitude damping at infinite temperature, to isolate the effect of zero-temperature bias in variational quantum circuits. The bias acts mainly through feature scale, and features shrink under both damping models. A trainable output scale removes most accuracy differences, but the cost reappears as additional measurement shots.

entry.title: Localising logical information in stabiliser codes using single-qubit measurements
entry.summary: Logical information localisation in stabiliser codes via single-qubit measurements arXiv · Oct 1, 2026This paper studies stabiliser path finding (SPF), a method for concentrating logical information from a stabiliser code with lost qubits onto a target qubit using one round of single-qubit measurements. It introduces g-SPF, which localises information onto at most g unspecified target qubits, and proves that for i.i.d. loss probability p<1/2 and large planar surface codes, this succeeds with probability tending to one, establishing a localisation threshold. The authors also present an exact integer linear programming algorithm and a faster heuristic decoding-based algorithm, validated on the surface code.

entry.title: Universal Inductive Inference of Quantum States: a framework for learning and predicting quantum sources from measurement data
entry.summary: Universal Inductive Inference of Quantum States arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper extends Solomonoff's universal inductive inference to quantum systems, introducing a framework for learning and predicting quantum sources that may have arbitrary correlations and entanglement across time. Given past measurement outcomes and post-measurement systems, the learner outputs a joint state predicting the next outcome while preserving correlations with past systems. The authors give an information-theoretic inference algorithm with round complexity O(sε⁻²δ⁻¹), prove a matching lower bound in the relevant regime, and construct a non-i.i.d. state tomography algorithm. They also investigate computational hardness under quantum cryptographic assumptions. ★★★★ Notable: Extends Solomonoff universal induction to quantum sources with arbitrary cross-time correlations and entanglement, giving an inference algorithm with round complexity O(sε^-2δ^-1) and reporting a matc

entry.title: Universal quantum coding using Schur-Weyl duality for error correction without prior channel knowledge
entry.summary: Universal quantum coding arXiv · Sep 30, 2026This paper addresses entanglement distillation from unknown noisy bipartite states and reliable quantum communication over noisy channels without prior knowledge of the state or channel. Using Schur-Weyl duality, the authors treat the irreducible permutation spaces from multiple copies of an unknown mixed state as maximally entangled code spaces and correct their symmetry-resolved errors. The work unifies entanglement distillation, quantum error correction and quantum communication within one representation-theoretic framework, with finite-copy guarantees. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use Schur-Weyl duality to build universal quantum codes needing no prior knowledge of the state or channel, unifying entanglement distillation and communication with claimed worst-case opt

entry.title: Transverse momentum as the counter-diabatic generator in bent waveguide couplers
entry.summary: Transverse momentum as the counter-diabatic generator in bent waveguide couplers arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies bent mode-evolution couplers, where bending the waveguide axis suppresses coupling between supermodes. The authors identify transverse momentum as the operator that generates the required counter-diabatic term. They derive a closed-form expression for the axis slope and compare the design with a straight coupler using a unitary transformation, reporting supermode fidelities of 0.994 and 1.000.

entry.title: A rigidity theorem: Gaussian states dominating separable operators are separable
entry.summary: Separability rigidity of Gaussian states under positive domination arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proves that a finite-mode Gaussian state is separable across a fixed mode partition if it dominates a nonzero positive operator that is separable across that partition. Three consequences follow: a Gaussian channel with a nonzero entanglement-breaking subchannel is entanglement breaking, and a connected graph of entangled two-mode Gaussian marginals certifies genuine multipartite entanglement. The authors also show full inseparability and genuine multipartite entanglement coincide for finite-mode Gaussian states. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a separability rigidity theorem for finite-mode Gaussian states: if a Gaussian state dominates a nonzero positive operator separable across a fixed partition, the state itself is sep

entry.title: Placement-driven reversal of preferred spin alignment in monolayer hBN vacancy pairs
entry.summary: Placement-driven reversal of preferred spin alignment in monolayer hBN vacancy pairs arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies how two negatively charged boron vacancies in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride align their spins when they interact. Using density-functional theory across seven configurations, the authors find that moving one vacancy by a single lattice vector reverses the preferred collinear spin alignment. The closest pair, 4.3 angstrom apart, favours parallel alignment, while a 7.5 angstrom pair favours antiparallel alignment.

entry.title: Quantum Networking at Quantum Computing Speed: Kilohertz Entanglement Between Different Quantum Systems
entry.summary: Quantum Networking at the Speed of Quantum Computation: Kilohertz Entanglement in a Heterogeneous Quantum System arXiv · Oct 8, 2026The paper entangles a trapped barium ion with a silicon-vacancy center in a diamond nanophotonic cavity. A photon from the ion is converted in wavelength and encoding, reflected off the cavity system, and detected, and one detected photon signals successful entanglement. Including all conversion losses, the average generation rate is 1.03 kHz, about one Bell pair per millisecond, matching the cycle time of planned trapped-ion processors. ★★★★ Notable: Entangles a trapped ion with a diamond SiV center at about 1 kHz, four times faster than prior ion-ion photonic links, shown experimentally.

entry.title: Equivalence of topological indices for U(1)⋊Z₂-symmetric quantum spin chains
entry.summary: The equivalence of topological indices for U(1)rtimesℤ₂-symmetric quantum spin chains arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper studies symmetry-protected topological phases in integer-spin quantum chains with on-site U(1)⋊Z₂ symmetry. It proves that Ogata's operator-algebraic index and Tasaki's elementary twist index are equivalent, giving an explicit error bound for computing the index. Combined with a boundary-field gap theorem and earlier calculations, it shows that the infinite S=1 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain has a symmetric gapped ground state with both indices equal to −1. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove equivalence of Ogata's and Tasaki's twist indices for U(1)⋊Z2 integer-spin chains with explicit error bound, and report both indices equal -1 for the infinite S=1 Heisenberg chain.

entry.title: Magnetic localization and spectral asymmetry of a charged particle near a screw dislocation
entry.summary: Magnetic localization and spectral asymmetry of a charged particle at a screw dislocation arXiv · Sep 27, 2026The paper studies a charged particle moving outside a screw dislocation in a uniform magnetic field. Although the geometry is locally Euclidean, the global screw identification couples conserved axial and azimuthal quantities. After separating cyclic coordinates, radial motion is governed by an inverse-square term and a magnetic harmonic confining term. For nonzero field strength the reduced problem is exactly solvable, giving an equally spaced spectrum with an orientation-dependent energy shift.

entry.title: Charging quantum batteries in a balanced loss-gain cavity pair
entry.summary: Charging Dicke and Tavis--Cummings quantum batteries with a PT-symmetric lossy--gain cavity pair arXiv · Oct 6, 2026This paper studies how a parity-time-symmetric photonic environment affects charging of Dicke and Tavis-Cummings quantum batteries. Each cavity holds an identical battery to keep the symmetry intact. In the broken phase the gain-side battery stores more energy, while in the unbroken phase it stores less than the lossy-side battery. The optimum lies on the broken side, near but not at the exceptional point.

entry.title: Minimal output entropy for box-adding or removing Young diagram channels, and a general Pauli principle
entry.summary: Minimal output entropy for the channels that add or remove a box of a Young diagram, and a Pauli principle for every permutation symmetry arXiv · Sep 27, 2026The paper studies four covariant quantum channels connecting irreducible U(d) representations whose Young diagrams differ by one box. The authors prove that for each channel, coherent states produce outputs that majorize all others, so coherent states minimize output entropy, and they give the optimal output explicitly using hook lengths. For the two channels that keep the box, they also identify all minimizers, which need not be coherent even when pure. Applied to N particles with a given permutation symmetry, the results give sharp bounds on the spectrum of a single particle's reduced density matrix and characterize the spectra reachable by mixed states; for fermions these recover the Pauli principle and Coleman's theorem.

entry.title: Exact Trotter error analysis for the degenerate quantum Rabi model
entry.summary: Exact Trotterization in the Degenerate Quantum Rabi Model arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies digital quantum simulation of the quantum Rabi model in the deep strong coupling regime, where Trotterization errors were previously known only through qualitative bounds. In the exactly solvable degenerate limit, the authors show that the first-order Trotter operator has a closed form and that the generated phase-space trajectory lies exactly on a rescaled, rotated circle. This yields a closed-form expression for state fidelity. They also report that promoting the Trotter-step coupling to a complex amplitude corrects this geometric error without additional circuit cost.

entry.title: Improved quantum algorithms for decomposing black-box Abelian groups into cyclic factors
entry.summary: Improved Quantum Algorithms for Black-Box Abelian Group Decomposition arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper presents a quantum algorithm that decomposes finite Abelian black-box groups into cyclic factors. It adapts quantum sampling and classical lattice reduction from Regev's factoring algorithm to compute an invariant-factor decomposition with high probability. Compared with the Cheung-Mosca approach, the authors report lower total gate counts, quantum time bounds, and qubit requirements.

entry.title: Collectivity: a mechanism that limits quantum entanglement even with long-range interactions
entry.summary: Collectivity limits quantum entanglement arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies how ground-state quantum entanglement is limited in gapped many-body systems with long-range power-law interactions. The authors show that many weak interactions produce fluctuations controlled by their square-summed strength, a mechanism they call collectivity. They derive logarithmic or subextensive entanglement bounds for arbitrary bipartitions and polylogarithmic bounds for regular bipartitions, and show several of these scalings are optimal. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show collectivity, not locality, limits entanglement under power-law interactions, reporting entanglement bounds and optimality results for long-range many-body systems.

entry.title: Observation of a topological defect state in the quantum Rabi model
entry.summary: Observation of a topological defect state in the quantum Rabi model arXiv · Sep 28, 2026This paper realizes a topological defect state of the quantum Rabi model, a spin coupled to an oscillator, using a single trapped 171Yb+ ion. Reconstructed phase-space distributions show centroid trajectories with windings of one and zero in two regimes as the coupling phase varies, linking discrete-lattice topology to the oscillator's continuous phase space. Measured spin responses to drive-amplitude modulation relate the stability of spin polarization to energy gaps and allowed transitions.

entry.title: A spectral threshold guaranteeing non-maximal Schmidt number
entry.summary: A threshold for maximal Schmidt number from spectrum arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper asks when the eigenvalue spectrum of a bipartite state on C^d⊗C^d alone ensures its Schmidt number is not maximal. Using spectral bounds for (d-1)-block positive operators, it proves that states whose largest eigenvalue does not exceed the sum of their p smallest eigenvalues, for p ≤ ⌊d²/2⌋, have Schmidt number at most d-1 under all global unitaries. It also shows that states satisfying the reduction criterion under arbitrary global unitaries belong to this class, while for d ≥ 3 it constructs maximal-Schmidt-number states satisfying the reduction criterion on both subsystems, showing the global unitary requirement is essential.

entry.title: Quantum data processing equality: a paper turning the quantum data processing inequality into an exact equality
entry.summary: Quantum data processing equality arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper promotes the quantum data processing inequality, which states that quantum relative entropy does not increase under quantum channels, to an exact equality using boundary and surface Poisson integral representations across a complex strip. The relative-entropy loss splits into two nonnegative components: a Petz recovery term governing state reconstructibility and a boundary term measuring mismatch of relative modular dynamics. The authors also establish recovery bounds at any prescribed modular parameter, with optimal square-root scaling in the relative entropy loss. ★★★★ Notable: Promotes the quantum data processing inequality to an exact equality via Poisson integral representations, decomposing the relative-entropy loss into Petz recovery and boundary terms.

entry.title: Discrete scale invariance in Ising mesons: how kink motion in a magnet gives log-periodic energy levels
entry.summary: Discrete Scale Invariance of Ising Mesons arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies composite excitations in a transverse-field Ising chain with long-range bonds decaying as 1/r^4. The authors show that dressed domain walls experience an asymptotic inverse-square attraction whose strength is set by spontaneous magnetization. The curvature of the dressed two-kink threshold sets the kinetic scale, and together these determine the scale-anomaly exponent and the meson hierarchy. Full-spin exact diagonalization and a fourth-order weak-field Hamiltonian are reported to support the coupled energy-size scaling in a finite window.

entry.title: Quantum codes with separate recovery locality for bit-flip and phase-flip errors
entry.summary: Asymmetric Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper introduces entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes with asymmetric locality, where bit-flip and phase-flip errors are corrected from recovery sets of different sizes. It extends a stabilizer-based sufficient condition and, in the CSS framework, places separate locality conditions on the two underlying classical codes. The authors derive Singleton-, Griesmer-, Plotkin-, sphere-packing-, and Cadambe–Mazumdar-type bounds for these codes. They also characterize when a pure CSS-type code built from two classical LRCs meets the Singleton-like bound with equality.

entry.title: Rényi channel capacity does not rise with non-signaling assistance
entry.summary: Monotonicity of the Rényi channel capacity under non-signaling assisted channel simulation arXiv · Sep 28, 2026The paper gives an alternative variational proof that shared non-signaling correlations between sender and receiver cannot increase the Rényi capacity of a classical channel. The result follows from a channel-divergence data-processing inequality by Oufkir, Yao and Berta, and uses a Legendre transform to write capacity as an extremum over affine functionals. Combined with separate arguments for Shannon capacity and endpoint orders, it establishes monotonicity for all orders. The authors also derive consequences for random-coding, sphere-packing and strong-converse exponents.

entry.title: Optimal Query Complexity for Preparing Ground States
entry.summary: Optimal Query Complexity for Ground-State Preparation arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper determines the optimal number of queries needed to prepare a quantum system's ground state to trace-distance error ε, given a known energy threshold in the spectral gap. It presents two algorithms, one with expected query count O((α/Δ)(γ⁻¹+log(1/ε))) and another with worst-case count O((α/(γΔ))log(1/ε)). A lower bound matching the expected query count is also proven. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report matching upper and lower bounds on ground-state preparation query complexity under a known energy threshold, with expected and worst-case query counts from spectral-filter purificat

entry.title: Estimating teleportation costs for distributed quantum chemistry circuits
entry.summary: Quantifying Teleportation Overhead in Distributed Unitary Coupled-Cluster Ansätze arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper estimates the resources needed to run unitary coupled-cluster circuits for hydrogen chains across distributed quantum processors using teleportation. It compares a naive distribution method with the TeleSABRE algorithm, counting Bell pairs and classical communication for nonlocal two-qubit gates. The authors find that UpCCD with spin-blocked Jordan-Wigner ordering scales most favorably, while UCCSD requires substantially more distributed resources.

entry.title: Two-copy measurements close the single-copy gap to the Holevo bound
entry.summary: Closing a single-copy gap to the Holevo bound with two-copy measurements arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies whether the Holevo Cramér-Rao bound for quantum multiparameter estimation can be attained with finite copies of a state. The authors construct a three-parameter rank-two model whose Holevo bound cannot be reached with one copy but is attained exactly with two, and they prove that full-rank models retain a finite-copy gap for any number of parameters. They also experimentally implement the two-copy collective measurement on superconducting qubits, observing error below single-copy and separate-measurement bounds, with this advantage persisting over a finite range of depolarizing noise. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct a three-parameter rank-two model where one copy cannot reach the Holevo bound but two copies do, and give a proof of finite-copy gap persistence for full-rank models, disproving

entry.title: Measurement-feedback interval can induce order in quantum Boltzmann samplers
entry.summary: Ordering controlled by the measurement-feedback interval in quantum Boltzmann samplers arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies whether changing only the measurement-feedback interval, with fixed couplings and a fixed local dissipative rule, can induce ordering in a quantum Boltzmann sampler. At zero environmental dephasing, repeated projective measurements remove transverse coherence regenerated during relaxation, enhancing the local longitudinal response. In the Curie–Weiss limit, for couplings below the equilibrium threshold, shortening the readout interval drives a continuous transition to an ordered stationary state even though the programmed Boltzmann distribution remains disordered.

entry.title: Quantum States and Spectra of Small Cylindrical and Toroidal Lattices
entry.summary: Quantum States and Spectra of Small Cylindrical and Toroidal Lattices arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the spectra and quantum states of small cylindrical and toroidal lattices under a scalar gauge potential that adds a position-dependent phase to inter-site coupling. Periodic boundary conditions generally break the gauge equivalence assumed for infinite lattices, and the authors identify conditions that restore it. They report gauge-dependent avoided crossings and persistent degeneracies, and examine the effects of boundary conditions, coupling strengths, and an axial field.

entry.title: Block-wise quantum algorithm for PDEs with interface penalties
entry.summary: Block-Wise Variational Quantum Algorithms for PDEs with Interface Penalty Constraints arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes a block-wise variational quantum algorithm for solving partial differential equations whose solutions vary in complexity across space. The domain is split into local quantum subproblems, with grid sizes and circuit designs assigned according to a computable difficulty indicator. Neighboring blocks are coupled through jump penalties on state values, derivatives, and fluxes, and the rough regions are adaptively tracked. Simulations on elliptic, advection-diffusion, and Burgers problems show lower errors and smaller peak local circuit width than global variational quantum approaches.

entry.title: Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction for Benzene Dimer Stacking Energies
entry.summary: A Divide-and-Conquer Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction for Evaluating π-π Stacking Interaction Energies in the Benzene Dimer arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes Divide-and-Conquer Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction (Deep QSCI) to evaluate π-π stacking interaction energies in the sandwich benzene dimer. QSCI is run on one monomer, and a reduced local basis built from its ground state is used to diagonalize an effective dimer Hamiltonian, reusing monomer results across monomers and distances to cut the required qubits from 40 to 20. With 6-31G**, the minimum is -0.91 kcal/mol at 4.0 Å, compared with -1.14 kcal/mol from counterpoise-corrected CCSD(T). With cc-pVDZ, large cancellations appear, which the authors suggest may stem from insufficient consistency of active orbitals and local bases between monomers.

entry.title: Optimizing randomized quantum simulation of Hamiltonians by minimizing average error
entry.summary: Optimized Randomized Hamiltonian Simulation via Average-Error Analysis arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper presents a framework for randomized Hamiltonian simulation that samples terms with arbitrary probabilities and implements their short-time evolutions in sequence. It shows that sampling in proportion to Hilbert-Schmidt norms, derived from Haar-averaged error bounds, can give smaller average-error bounds than the standard qDRIFT method. For Pauli-string Hamiltonians, combining this with commuting Pauli grouping further reduces error bounds at fixed depth.

entry.title: Single-photon nonlinearity from a quantum dot in a nanobeam cavity
entry.summary: Single-Photon Nonlinearity from a Nanobeam with a Quantum Dot arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper reports a single-photon nonlinearity built from a nanobeam cavity coupled to one quantum dot. The device couples directly to a single-mode fiber with 60% efficiency and reaches the nonlinearity at a threshold of 0.24 incident photons per resonant picosecond pulse. The system operates in the strong-coupling regime, with a coupling rate g/2π of 29.1 GHz and cooperativity C of 3.98. The authors present it as a compact, chip-integrable, fiber-compatible building block for photonic quantum technologies.

entry.title: Synchronizing quantum devices over lossy channels using polarization assistance
entry.summary: Synchronized Quantum Devices in Lossy Channels arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a polarization-assisted protocol that uses entangled photon pairs to keep quantum devices synchronized under high channel loss, such as satellite-to-ground links. The experiments show reliable synchronization at higher losses and up to a 40% increase in satellite-to-ground distance. Monte Carlo simulations indicate the improvement holds across a wide range of photon-starved conditions.

entry.title: Root-system structure of sloppiness in passive Gaussian metrology
entry.summary: Root-system structure of sloppiness in passive Gaussian metrology arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper studies when passive transformations of squeezed Gaussian probes become locally unidentifiable because the quantum Fisher matrix loses rank. It shows that the C_n restricted-root system of Sp(2n,R)/U(n) governs this exact sloppiness for pure zero-mean Gaussian probes. It also solves the E-optimal probe-design problem of maximizing the smallest passive Fisher eigenvalue at fixed mean photon number.

entry.title: Shared phase arithmetic: applying a layer of diagonal quantum rotations at once
entry.summary: Shared Phase Arithmetic for Parallel Quantum Rotations arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proposes parallel phase kickback (PPK), which coherently computes a weighted sum of several rotation parameters, adds it once to a phase-gradient state, and then uncomputes it. This separates the cost of representing a phase function from the cost of applying it. The authors prove correctness, give explicit error bounds, and analyze logical gate counts for general weights, pairs of rotations, and weights with disjoint binary support. The bounds show when shared phase arithmetic reduces amortized rotation cost and when encoding overhead limits that advantage.

entry.title: A paper on how quantum Fisher information and quantum coherence factorize over time
entry.summary: Factorization dynamics between quantum Fisher information and quantum coherence arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the factorization relationship between quantum Fisher information, which measures how sensitive a quantum state is to parameter changes, and quantum coherence. The authors prepared pure states in qubit and qutrit systems, applied unitary evolution, and confirmed the factorization law both theoretically and experimentally. They also derived a lower bound on the variance of the estimated parameter that does not require final-state information.

entry.title: A general spin-chain method for multicomponent anyons in 1D optical lattices
entry.summary: Generalized Effective Spin-Chain formalism for multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper introduces a generalized effective spin-chain (GESC) framework for strongly interacting multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices. It maps particle motion to spinless fermions and spin states to an ordered chain, separating spin and charge degrees of freedom. The authors report that in the strong-interaction regime the fractional exchange phase appears in spin-exchange coefficients through virtual tunneling. They also describe how direction-dependent phases affect non-equilibrium impurity transport.

entry.title: Multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices: a study of how particles with fractional exchange statistics behave in a 1D lattice
entry.summary: Multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies the ground-state and dynamical behavior of multicomponent interacting anyons confined in a one-dimensional optical lattice, using the Anyon-Hubbard model. It shows that fractional exchange statistics combined with multicomponent effects reshape charge and spin correlations, including asymmetric momentum-distribution shells and new peaks. The authors report antiferromagnetic spin ordering and find that the statistical phase parameter can switch dipole oscillations between underdamped and overdamped regimes.

entry.title: Emergent symmetries after ensemble averaging: a review of how global symmetries can arise in quantum gravity.
entry.summary: Emergent Symmetries in Ensemble Averages arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper reviews work showing that global symmetries, believed absent in quantum gravity, can emerge after ensemble averages of theories as encountered in holography. Its case study is the ensemble average of two-dimensional Narain-type conformal field theories with an even quadratic form, computed by the Siegel-Weil formula and interpreted as a sum over geometries in a three-dimensional Abelian Chern-Simons theory. The authors also relate this to the Swampland program and recast strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking of mixed states as symmetry emergence in ensemble averages, motivating a new Swampland conjecture.

entry.title: Quantum References Beat Classical Ones for Leakage Detection
entry.summary: Exponential Advantage of Quantum over Classical References in Leakage Detection arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper shows that leakage from an encoding subspace can be detected using independent quantum reference states prepared by the same encoder, without a classical description of the encoding. For orthogonal leakage, the miss probability is asymptotically 4/M, independent of the ambient dimension. Measuring all references first yields zero detection under the same zero-false-alarm requirement. For one logical qubit in three physical qubits, seven coherent references achieve at least 50% detection, while a measurement-first receiver needs at least 588. ★★★★ Notable: Proposes detecting leakage with independent quantum references from the same encoder, needing no classical encoding description; the authors prove optimality under zero false alarm and report that for

entry.title: Factorization of driven anisotropic Rabi–Stark Hamiltonians via affine spin pencils
entry.summary: Affine spin-pencil factorization of generalized driven anisotropic Rabi--Stark Hamiltonians in an inhomogeneous orthosymplectic superalgebra arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper constructs a supersymmetric factorization of generalized driven anisotropic Rabi–Stark Hamiltonians using an affine factor in an inhomogeneous orthosymplectic superalgebra. The normal product has an exact zero-energy ground doublet and a Witten index of two. It also covers a Bargmann hierarchy, endpoint conditions for exceptional finite-polynomial states, several limiting cases, and an interior example with additional drives, Stark deformation and intensity-dependent coupling.

entry.title: Evanescent-wave Johnson noise from superconductors, explained
entry.summary: Evanescent-wave Johnson Noise from Superconductors arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper calculates evanescent-wave Johnson noise above a superconductor's surface and the resulting relaxation time T1 of spin and charge qubits placed nanometers away. It uses a microscopic current-response kernel for a BCS superconductor, together with the fluctuation-dissipation theorem and nonlocal surface impedances. Magnetic noise is enhanced just below Tc by the coherence peak and falls exponentially at lower temperatures, while magnetic impurities produce a zero-temperature noise floor. ★★★★ Notable: Presents a theory of evanescent-wave Johnson noise and near-surface qubit T1 above superconductors, predicting a magnetic-noise coherence peak below Tc, a zero-temperature noise floor from magnetic im

entry.title: How work cumulants scale when a driven Gaussian field crosses over between regimes
entry.summary: Crossover of Scaling Behaviors of Work Cumulants in a Driven Gaussian Field Theory arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper derives the finite-temperature characteristic function of work for a driven O(N) Gaussian field theory and gives closed-form expressions for all zero-temperature excess-work cumulants. For gapped protocols, adiabatic perturbation theory yields a τ_Q^-2 scaling, where τ_Q is the protocol duration. For power-law protocols approaching criticality, the authors analyze the competition between critical excitations and regular contributions, identifying Kibble–Zurek-type scaling and a logarithmic correction at a specific threshold.

entry.title: Dynamical resource theory of time-reversal symmetry breaking
entry.summary: Dynamical resource theory of time-reversal symmetry breaking arXiv · Sep 29, 2026The paper proposes an operationally meaningful framework for quantifying the intrinsic time-reversal symmetry breaking (T-violation) of quantum channels, treating it as a resource within dynamical resource theory. T-violation is split into kinematic T-violation, arising from antiunitary motion-reversal, and nonunitality driven purely by thermodynamics. The authors also analyze the resulting resource theory of kinematic T-violation and report a universal golden unit, including for classical channels.

entry.title: Puncturing method for adaptive entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes
entry.summary: Puncturing for Adaptive Entanglement-Assisted Stabilizer Codes arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper extends a puncturing construction for standard stabilizer codes to entanglement-assisted codes, so that one mother code can be adjusted to different numbers of available pre-shared Bell pairs. The three-step procedure treats the code as unassisted, punctures one receiver-side qubit, and recovers an entanglement-assisted form, reducing the required Bell pairs by one while keeping transmitted and logical qubit counts. The authors derive a bound on the resulting distance loss and give conditions for preserving the original distance. In an analysis of random codes with five to eight transmitted qubits, 14.75% had greater distance than their unassisted counterparts, and 81.4% of those admitted a puncturing choice that keeps the original distance.

entry.title: Bivariate bicycle codes over group algebras: quantum codes built from weighted shifts
entry.summary: Bivariate Bicycle Codes over Group Algebras arXiv · Sep 29, 2026This paper studies bivariate bicycle group-algebra (BBGA) quantum error-correcting codes built from weighted shift operators over finite group algebras. The authors give sparsity bounds and present computer-verified examples, including a [[144,16,12]] code over a nonabelian group and a [[18,4,3]] code. They show these examples are inequivalent to ordinary abelian realizations.
